_comment: bootstrap's four Roles. A lane of a Process diagram names the Role its tasks are performed in, with BPMN's own partitionElementRef pointing at a bpmn:resource whose id is the Role's id. The lane is not the Role (owner, 2026-10-16). An Actor takes the Role on for the length of that lane. Roles are declared here, rather than left as lane names in the diagrams, so that every lane names a Role somebody defined. A Role played by a mechanical Actor is as real as any other, and its skills are its contract.
name: bootstrap

roles.title: Bootstrapping Agent
roles.description: An agent asked to set up a Harness with ONLY the knowledge bootstrap's README.md hands it. That constraint is the role, not a caveat on it: a Bootstrapping Agent has no MCP server, no harness, no work plan and no skills beyond those bootstrap carries, and a step that assumes any of those is a step a Bootstrapping Agent cannot perform. It stops being a Bootstrapping Agent the moment the harness is installed and it re-enters through that harness instead.
roles.persona: Knows nothing about this repository and cannot look anything up. Reads files, follows the processes bootstrap carries, and asks exactly one question when it must — `discussion` is how that asking is performed and what it must produce.

roles.title: Knowledge Graph Data Store
roles.description: A git repository, reached either through the git CLI or through a forge's API. It is where a declaration and its graph are READ from and where a new layer's declaration is WRITTEN to. It holds and serves, and takes no part in deciding what should happen. Its skill is its contract, `knowledge-graph-data-store`: what it must serve and keep, which a test can check.

roles.title: Requestor
roles.description: Wants to initialize — or bootstrap, or install, or load, or harness — a harness: bootstrap itself, or any Harness built on it. Carries no skills deliberately: WHICH harness this repository should become is a judgement about intent, and no instruction body produces it. The Bootstrapping Agent may narrow the list from context; only the Requestor settles it.

roles.title: Logger
roles.description: A machine that accepts log messages and puts them somewhere a person can read. It receives and records, and takes no part in what happens next. Its skill is its contract, `logger`: record a complete message unchanged and attributed to its actor. Composing the message is `log-message`, the skill of whoever is doing the thing being logged.
